newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Ropczyce sugar firm to gain investor Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: Polish Ropczyce sugar firm to gain investor Feb 14.

text.p: The main shareholder of Poland's largest sugar refinery, Ropczyce, will choose an investor to take a 38-percent stake in the sugar maker on February 14, the president of sugar holding Lubelska Spolka Cukrowa said.

Stanislaw Misztal, head of Lubelska Spolka Cukrowa which has 51 percent of Ropczyce, told Reuters on Wednesday that eight foreign and domestic firms had bid in the tender worth about 50 million zlotys.
"The tender will be decided this Friday -- we've received eight offers and we're in the process of appraising the submitted documents," Misztal said.
He said the tender included a new share issue, after which the investor would have 38 percent of Ropczyce, Lubelska Spolka Cukrowa about 32 percent and the state treasury 30 percent.
Misztal said Rolimpex, Denmark's Danisco A/S ,, France's Eridania Beghin-Say and Generale Sucriere, Germany's Sudzucker, the Netherlands' Cosun and Britain's Tate and Lyle and British Sugar had bid.
Ropczyce, which has not released earnings figures, produced 58,000 tonnes of sugar last year.
